 FAA issues ground stop for all flights due to ‘extraordinary circumstances’

 FAA issues ground stop for all flights due to ‘extraordinary circumstances’ 
 4:20
 Ad Feedback 
 What's happening now
 • Ground stop: All flights in the United States are grounded until further notice , “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the Federal Aviation Administration said. The issue stems from a telecommunications outage , but an airline source told CNN the root cause is still unclear .
 • No known threat: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the ground stop did not stem from a threat to the US and was not linked to this week’s disruptive Microsoft outage. Preliminary reports indicate this was not a cyberattack , law enforcement sources told CNN. President Donald Trump has been briefed .
 • No timetable for resolution: Mullin warned that a resolution will take time . News of the rare nationwide ground stop is trickling in to passengers at major airports across the country as airlines start to share updates about delays and cancellations.

 Student pilot has to land plane solo, atc audio shows 
 1:10
 “I don’t know what to do,” a student pilot told air traffic controllers during the nationwide ground stop on Friday.
 Controllers at the Fort Worth Meacham International Airport tower advised the pilot he needed to land the aircraft and asked where he would like to land.
 The plane landed a few minutes at Hicks Airfield, about 15 miles northwest of Fort Worth, after the pilot’s conversation with the controller, according to FlightAware.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 6:15 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 After roughly two hours, the nationwide ground stop is still in effect, FAA says
 By Nicki Brown 
 Passengers pass a screen showing departures at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington, DC on Friday. 
 Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images 
 Planes across the country are still barred from taking off roughly two hours after a nationwide ground stop was issued, according to an advisory from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
 As facilities begin to recover, flights will be allowed to depart once they coordinate with the FAA’s command center located in Virginia, according to the update.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 6:13 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Trump’s top aides monitoring and seeking answers over nationwide groundstop
 By Kaitlan Collins 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth were both in and out of the West Wing Friday as officials scrambled to respond to a nationwide ground stop of flights.
 Hegseth was in the Situation Room, a person familiar with the matter told CNN, as Mullin briefly stepped outside to answer reporters’ questions.
 Mullin said President Donald Trump had been briefed by officials on the FAA ground stop for all flights and had spoken on the phone with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
 That urgency wasn’t apparent across government social media accounts, namely the president’s.
 The president posted on Truth Social about an effort to provide tax incentives to help revitalize the US entertainment industry, and about a Coast Guard rescue from a crash between two ships in Louisiana.

 Customers set to fly this evening should expect delays and cancellations, JetBlue says
 By Eduardo Cuevas 
 JetBlue customers scheduled to fly this evening should expect delays and cancellations, the airline said in a statement.
 JetBlue has temporarily suspended all departures, the airline said, adding flights already in the air are continuing to destinations.
 “Safety remains our top priority, and we are working closely with the FAA as we monitor the situation,” JetBlue said. The airline said customers should check flight status at jetblue.com or the JetBlue app for the latest information.

 No flights have left from some major airports in several hours
 By August Phillips 
 Passengers wait at boarding gates at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Washington, DC on Friday. 
 Zina Desmazes/AFP/Getty Images 
 No flights have taken off from Chicago O’Hare International Airport in over two hours, according to flight-tracking service Flightradar24, amid the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop.
 Several other major US airports have also not seen any planes leave since before 4 p.m. ET, according to a Flightradar24 post at 5:25 p.m.
 The last recorded takeoffs at both New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport were at 3:35 p.m., according to the tracker.

 FAA "doesn't know yet what is going on," according to source
 By Pete Muntean 
 The FAA “doesn’t know yet what is going on; it is affecting different facilities in different ways,” an airline source told CNN. “Ten minutes ago, they were on a crisis call and there was still no clear answer as to a cause.”

 United Airlines notifies passengers about ground stop in app
 By Jeff Simon , Alexandra Skores and Nicki Brown 
 from United Airlines 
 United Airlines, one of the country’s biggest airlines, notified passengers about the nationwide ground stop in a statement on its app and advised them to keep an eye out for updates.
 “Due to a nationwide ground stop by the FAA, we’re holding planes from taking off at this time,” the airline said in the statement. “Planes already in flight will continue.”
 “We’ll update you as we learn more,” the statement said.
 In a statement to CNN, United Airlines said new domestic flights will not take off while the ground stop is in place, but airborne flights will continue.
 “United will work with our customers to get them to their destinations once this issue is resolved,” the airline said.
 CNN’s Chris Isidore contributed to this report.

 Passenger stuck on tarmac at Chicago airport for more than 2 hours after nationwide ground stop was issues
 1:13
 • Source:

 Passenger stuck on tarmac at Chicago airport for more than 2 hours after nationwide ground stop was issues 
 1:13
 Jerry Bovard landed in Chicago earlier this afternoon expecting to deplane and go home.
 But what he expected would be a two minute experience eventually turned into hours of sitting on the tarmac after a nationwide ground stop was announced.
 “It’s definitely a mess,” Bovard told CNN’s Isabel Rosales. “I was just happy to be home and then we sat there for two and a half hours so not a good way to end things.”

 Here’s how travelers and pilots are reacting to the national ground stop
 CNN staff
 After a national ground stop was issued blocking all planes from taking off, the announcement trickled down to travelers across the country who were caught up in thousands of delays and some cancellations while trying to figure out how long it might last.
 On a plane scheduled to depart from John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York to Savannah, Georgia, passengers were informed of the ground stop shortly before expected takeoff. The pilot said he was mandated by the FAA to provide updates but had nothing new to share, adding they would wait for some time before returning to the gate.
 The mood among passengers was grim as they waited, hoping for good news, while flight attendants passed out snacks.
 At Chicago O’Hare International Airport, communication to travelers about the ground stop didn’t appear to be straightforward, and travelers seemed relaxed and unaware of the scope of the advisory. One airline simply told passengers there was a “delay” and offered a meal voucher for passengers on one flight with an email saying, “We’re sorry about the change to your travel plans.”
 Periodically, a gate agent announced there was a ground stop but didn’t offer further context.
 One traveler on a flight to Los Angeles told CNN they only learned of the ground stop through the news and did not hear an announcement on their flight. Meanwhile, passengers on a flight that had already taken off were worried about whether they could land.
 A pilot who was airborne said many pilots are reverting to the emergency frequency given the magnitude of the radio frequency outages. One FAA controller at an air traffic control center told CNN, “It’s a hot mess right now.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:43 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Outages include air traffic control radars and radio frequencies, source says
 By René Marsh 
 People wait in Terminal B during a nationwide ground stop at Orlando International Airport on Friday. 
 Finn Gomez/Getty Images 
 The outages across the country involve air traffic control radars as well as radio frequencies simultaneously going out, according to an aviation source familiar with what controllers are dealing with.
 Controllers do not have any clarity on the cause and what exactly is going on, the source said.
 Last year, controllers handling flights approaching or departing from Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey had multiple radar and communication outages when problems with a copper cable carrying the information led to communication blackouts.
 As a result, multiple controllers took trauma leave, which exacerbated already short staffing and led to long delays and cancellations. The cable that failed was eventually replaced with a fiberoptic cable, according to the Department of Transportation .
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:42 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Southwest Airlines says it's working with the FAA to resolve the issue
 By Pete Muntean 
 Passengers queue at the Southwest Airlines desk to speak with a representative at Eppley Airfield in Omaha, Nebraska., on Friday. 
 Nikos Frazier/Omaha World-Herald/Getty Images 
 Southwest Airlines told employees tonight that it is working with the Federal Aviation Administration to solve the communication issue causing the nationwide ground stop.
 “We are aware of the current nationwide ground stop and are actively working with the FAA for resolution,” the airline said in a message to its employees.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:39 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Ground stop could have “a cascading effect for air travel for some time,” analyst says
 By Tori B. Powell 
 There’s “no real end in sight” for the flight delays and cancellations being reported throughout the country amid the nationwide ground stop currently in effect, according to CNN aviation correspondent Pete Muntean.
 He told CNN’s Jake Tapper flight cancellations and delays throughout the country are increasing and could continue to do so for some time.
 “This is not going to be a short-haul story. This is going to last at least likely until tonight,” Muntean said. “It’s very difficult for airlines to reset after a huge widespread issue like this.”
 He warned the ground stop could have “a cascading effect for air travel for some time to come.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:32 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Ranking member of aviation subcommittee calls for investigation into ground stop
 By Aleena Fayaz 
 Sen. Tammy Duckworth today called for a “thorough and complete” investigation into the nationwide ground stop.
 “The safety of our skies is built on redundancies. Whatever led to the nationwide ground stop will warrant a thorough and complete investigation,” Duckworth wrote in a post on X , adding, “I’ll be demanding answers from the FAA.”
 Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois, serves as the ranking member of the Senate Subcommittee on Aviation.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:26 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 At JFK, queued passengers call loved ones as they await more information
 By Zachary Slater 
 Some passengers flying to Savannah, Georgia, waited on a tarmac at John F. Kennedy International Airport for 90 minutes before an update came.
 Following the long wait, the pilot finally announced that it was not immediately clear what would happen next.
 Frustrated passengers peppered tired flight attendants with questions, asking about how checked bags would be retrieved if the plane returns to the gate and how the ground stop could impact flights tomorrow.
 Row by row, passengers called friends and family to let them know they probably won’t make it to their destination tonight.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:25 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 “Safety is always our top priority,” says Airlines for America
 By Emma Tucker 
 Airlines for America, the major trade association representing US airlines, said it’s in close communication with the Department of Transportation and the FAA regarding the nationwide ground stop, adding: “Safety is always our top priority.”
 “We appreciate the patience of the traveling public and the dedication of frontline employees who are navigating this situation.”
 The association encouraged impacted travelers to be in touch with their carrier for “real-time updates.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:19 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Ground stop caused by "temporary telecommunications outage," FAA says
 By Dalia Faheid 
 An airplane prepares to land at Miami International Airport on Friday. 
 Marco Bello/Reuters 
 The Federal Aviation Administration said the nationwide ground stop today was caused by a “temporary telecommunications outage.”
 The statement comes about an hour after Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop.
 The agency said “out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted.”
 All flights have been accounted for and international flights “will be handled on a case by case basis,” the FAA said.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:20 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 American Airlines says flights expected to be disrupted for the rest of the day
 By Tori B. Powell 
 Airplanes are parked on the tarmac at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on Friday. 
 Jonathan Ernst/Reuters 
 American Airlines flights are expected to face disruptions for the rest of the day depending on how long the nationwide ground stop currently in effect will last, the company said in a statement.
 “It will be all hands-on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop,” American Airlines said.
 Flights already in the air can still continue to their destinations, the company added.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:18 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 No time frame in place to resolve communications outage, Mullin says
 By Kevin Liptak 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials have not yet discussed a time frame for resolving the FAA communications outage as the administration focuses on passenger safety.
 “We have not discussed any timeframe,” he told reporters at the White House.
 “It’s going to take some time,” he went on. “And so this isn’t going to just be resolved and turned around within the hour.”

 Some ‘people appear to be unaware’: CNN reports across US airports amid FAA nationwide ground stop
 2:59
 • Source:
 CNN 
 Some ‘people appear to be unaware’: CNN reports across US airports amid FAA nationwide ground stop 
 2:59
 At Chicago O’Hare International Airport, the mood remains relaxed. There’s a feeling the customers don’t grasp the extent of this nationwide ground stop.
 ANA Airlines offered a meal voucher for the two-hour delay to a flight from O’Hare to Haneda Airport in Tokyo with an email saying “we’re sorry about the change to your travel plans.”
 Periodically, a gate agent will announce there’s a ground stop but provide no further context. It feels like a minor inconvenience. People are sitting down waiting on the delay to be done.
 There’s no lines with gate agents. The only line of folks I’m seeing is for a Lufthansa flight that had customers line up to board.
 Traveler Karthik Digavalli, who was planning on flying to India with family after a layover at Frankfurt Airport, said he found out about the ground stop through chatter on X.
 “It was pretty calm. I think people were just starting to understand what’s going on,” he said.
 Passengers on the flight were told they would soon receive an update on the flight status.
 “We’ll see how it goes,” he said. “I just hope everything gets resolved soon.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:14 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 FAA issues and Microsoft outage are not connected, Mullin says
 By Molly English 
 Passengers look at departures and arrivals boards at Logan International Airport in Boston on Friday. 
 Brian Snyder/Reuters 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that yesterday’s massive global Microsoft outage and the communications problem causing today’s national FAA ground stop are not connected.
 “I don’t see any reason to connect those two at all,” Mullin told reporters at the White House Friday afternoon. “Those are separate issues.”
 Yesterday’s outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, affected millions globally and left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life . AI companies said they were facing issues as well. Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products .
